trust_decision.summary: A peer-supplied packet line whose payload is only the side-band designator (e.g. 0005\x02) must yield empty text without panicking; decided in gix-packetline's two low-level primitives decode_band() and TextRef::from() (lib.rs), which both side-band readers call, with the reachable trigger being the 1-byte payload shape.

landing_point.why: The summary names an 'empty side-band packet', and decode_band() is the only public operation that turns a data line into a band; it indexes d[0] and slices &d[1..] without a length check.

fix_sites.entry_point: PacketLineRef::decode_band() (public; called by both side-band readers)
impl From<&[u8]> for TextRef, used by PacketLineRef::as_text()

fix_sites.module_kind: async reader implementation (parallel copy of the blocking one)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: TextRef::from is framed as a trailing-newline text helper used by handshake code in other packages, not as part of side-band decoding, and our own serializer refuses to emit an empty payload (gix-packetline/src/blocking_io/encode.rs:93), so a solver who reproduces through the writer concludes the shape is unreachable and fixes only decode_band or only the blocking reader.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A data-band line with an empty payload (0005\x01) is a legitimate keep-alive under sideband-all and is skipped, while an empty progress/error payload must still be forwarded to the progress handler as empty text; a fix that treats any payload-less band line as malformed, or that errors on empty progress text, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: empty packet-line payload constructed by API users: PacketLineRef::Data(b"")
one-byte payload that is only the band designator: 0005\x02 and 0005\x03 (empty progress/error text)
one-byte payload for the data band: 0005\x01 (legitimate keep-alive, must be skipped)
band text with and without a trailing newline (TextRef strips one)
reader buffer shorter than the 4-byte hex prefix (the read.rs guard)

O7_producer.where: gix-packetline/src/blocking_io/encode.rs:81-95 and gix-packetline/src/async_io/encode.rs:213 (band_to_write), which reject an empty payload with DataIsEmpty, so the trigger shape exists only on the wire from a hand-crafted peer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: as_band(Channel) takes the whole slice without validating or stripping a designator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the sibling decoder next to decode_band and a maintainer could make it slice &d[1..] for symmetry, reintroducing the same unchecked index.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: peek_buffer_replace_and_truncate indexes self.peek_buf[position] with a peer-derived position
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The position comes from scanning a server line for a NUL byte in gix-transport/src/client/capabilities.rs:216, so the same 'trust the length' mistake is idiomatic there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the v0/v1 handshake calls as_text() on the first line the server sends
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the pre-auth entry point the advisory describes; a maintainer hardening the handshake would add its own emptiness check rather than the one in lib.rs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: lines read from an external filter process are passed to as_text()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a second transport into the same text conversion, in another package, with an equally untrusted peer.

O9_family: unchecked index / length arithmetic on attacker-controlled packet payload (CWE-191 shape, slice panic) leading to a remote DoS

O10_build.project_tests: gix-packetline/tests/{decode/mod.rs,read/mod.rs,read/sideband.rs,encode/mod.rs,write/mod.rs} plus tests/blocking-packetline.rs and tests/async-packetline.rs, driven by maybe-async; they feed in-memory byte slices, no network. The fix adds tests to tests/decode/mod.rs and tests/read/sideband.rs, neither of which exists in the pinned tree.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an emptiness check only at the blocking side-band reader (or only in decode_band) and validate through the same reader, leaving TextRef::from and the async reader's copy untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: gix-packetline/fuzz/fuzz_targets/packet_lines.rs:19-22 works around the panic with `if !data.is_empty()` before calling as_text()/decode_band(); it is a harness guard, not a product fix, and was not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured without shell access; the workspace lists ~70 crates so tiny_repo/giant_repo were judged inapplicable.

The two read.rs length guards are unreachable through the public API (read_line()/peek_line() always pass a MAX_LINE_LEN buffer, gix-packetline/src/blocking_io/read.rs:141-143 and :168), so no route exercises that hunk; stated from reading, not from running.

Caveat rather than a gap: gix-packetline is a small, easily read crate, so the 'too large to read whole' lever does not apply here; difficulty rests on the two sinks, the blocking/async duplication and the keep-alive trap.
